title: Claude Martin was born
description: The French soldier and adventurer who later built Lucknow's Constantia palace and founded La Martiniere College was born in Lyon.

title: Birju Maharaj died
description: The Kathak maestro of Lucknow's Kalka-Bindadin gharana died in Delhi, mourned across India's classical arts world.

title: K. D. Singh 'Babu' was born
description: The two-time Olympic gold-medallist hockey forward, celebrated as one of the game's finest dribblers, was born in Barabanki and built his career and reputation in Lucknow.

title: Birju Maharaj was born
description: The dancer, composer and singer became the leading exponent of Lucknow's Kalka-Bindadin Kathak gharana, popularising the city's classical dance tradition worldwide.

title: Awadh was annexed by the East India Company
description: The annexation ended the reign of Wajid Ali Shah, the last King of Awadh.

title: Josh Malihabadi died
description: The Malihabad-born poet died in Islamabad, having migrated to Pakistan in 1956.

title: Talat Mahmood was born in Lucknow
description: The playback singer and actor, known as the 'King of Ghazals', was born in Lucknow.

title: Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Calcutta
description: Following the annexation of Awadh, the deposed Nawab was sent into exile at Garden Reach, Calcutta, where he lived out his life as a patron of the arts.

title: The foundation of Charbagh railway station was laid
description: Bishop George Herbert laid the foundation of Lucknow's landmark Charbagh station, an Indo-Saracenic building completed in 1923.

title: K. D. Singh 'Babu' died in Lucknow
description: The Olympic hockey legend died at his Lucknow home; the city's main sports stadium in Hazratganj was later named in his honour.

title: Begum Hazrat Mahal died in exile
description: The regent who led Lucknow's resistance during the 1857 uprising died in Kathmandu, having refused British amnesty.

title: Naushad Ali died
description: The Lucknow-born composer, one of the most influential figures in Hindi film music, died in Mumbai.

title: Talat Mahmood died
description: The Lucknow-born singer died in Mumbai after a career spanning playback singing and acting.

title: The 1857 uprising reached Lucknow
description: Mutiny broke out in Lucknow as the wider uprising spread across north India.

title: The Battle of Chinhat was fought near Lucknow
description: Rebel forces defeated the East India Company force near Chinhat and Ismailganj.

title: The siege of the Lucknow Residency began
description: The Residency became the centre of a prolonged siege during the uprising of 1857.

title: Birjis Qadr was proclaimed Nawab of Awadh in Lucknow
description: Begum Hazrat Mahal had her eleven-year-old son declared ruler and governed Awadh in his name through the rebellion.

title: Wajid Ali Shah was born in Lucknow
description: The future last King of Awadh was born in Lucknow.

title: Begum Hazrat Mahal was honoured in Hazratganj, Lucknow
description: A commemoration at Old Victoria Park recognised her leadership of the 1857 resistance from Lucknow; the park was later renamed for her.

title: Atal Bihari Vajpayee died
description: The former Prime Minister, who represented Lucknow in the Lok Sabha for over a decade, died in New Delhi.

title: Claude Martin died in Lucknow
description: The founder of La Martiniere College died in the city; per his wishes the college marks the date as Founder's Day rather than a day of mourning.

title: The first relief force resumed its advance toward Lucknow
description: Henry Havelock's force resumed its advance toward the besieged Residency.

title: Havelock and Outram marched toward Lucknow
description: The relief force continued its advance toward the besieged Residency.

title: Asaf-ud-Daula died in Lucknow
description: The Nawab who built the Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza died and was buried within the Bara Imambara complex.

title: The relief force reached Alambagh
description: Havelock's force drove rebel forces from Alambagh during its advance on Lucknow.

title: The first relief of Lucknow reached the Residency
description: Havelock and Outram's force fought through the city and reached the Residency.

title: La Martiniere College, Lucknow began classes
description: The school opened with 70 boys inside Claude Martin's Constantia palace, following years of litigation over his will.

title: Begum Akhtar was born
description: The singer known as 'Mallika-e-Ghazal' was born Akhtari Bai Faizabadi; she later lived, performed and was buried in Lucknow.

title: Mirza Hadi Ruswa died
description: The Lucknow-born writer of 'Umrao Jan Ada', often called the first modern Urdu novel and set among the city's tawaif culture, died in Hyderabad.

title: Begum Akhtar died
description: The ghazal, dadra and thumri singer died in Ahmedabad after her final performance; she is buried in Lucknow's Thakurganj area.

title: The second relief of Lucknow reached the Residency
description: Colin Campbell's relief operation enabled the evacuation of the Residency.

title: Women and children were evacuated from Lucknow
description: Civilians were evacuated following the second relief of the Residency.

title: British forces withdrew from the Lucknow Residency
description: The Residency was abandoned after the evacuation.

title: The University of Lucknow was established
description: Built on the foundation of the older Canning College, the University of Lucknow was formally founded.

title: Josh Malihabadi was born
description: The Urdu poet, known as 'Shayar-e-Inquilab', was born Shabbir Hasan Khan at Malihabad, near Lucknow.

title: Naushad Ali was born in Lucknow
description: The pioneering Hindi film composer, later honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, was born and raised in Lucknow.

title: Gandhi and Nehru's first meeting is traditionally placed at Lucknow
description: Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru are said to have first met during the Indian National Congress session held at Lucknow's Charbagh station grounds.

title: The Lucknow Pact was adopted
description: The Indian National Congress, meeting in Lucknow, adopted the pact with the All India Muslim League on constitutional reform and communal representation; the League ratified it two days later.
